programName: Bachelor of Applied Science (BASc) in Computer Engineering
programDescription: Building on a solid foundation of traditional engineering skills, this program covers many different aspects of computer software and hardware design, and allows for more specialized studies in microprocessor-based systems, computer architecture, programming concepts, real-time operating systems, software engineering, and robotics. Computer Engineering is a specialized discipline that combines electrical engineering and computer science. Computer engineers are responsible for ensuring the safe operation of information systems — they are expert designers of computers and their digital components, as well as expert in the design and analysis of control systems based on computers, and in the design of large communication networks. Throughout the program, students take non-engineering courses covering communication skills, economics, ethical issues, and the impact of technology on society. First-year compulsory courses include: Principles of Chemistry, Engineering Mechanics, Fundamentals of Engineering Computation, Digital Systems I, Introduction to Computing II, Calculus I, and Calculus II. Technical elective options in upper years include: wireless networks, applied machine learning for computer engineering, distributed systems design, digital image processing, computer network management, design of secure computer systems, and computer control in robotics. All courses are available in English and French.
admissionCoursesNeeded:
ENG4U (English) or FRA4U (French)
MHF4U (Advanced Functions)
MCV4U (Calculus and Vectors)
SPH4U (Physics)
SCH4U (Chemistry)

livingCostDetails: Off-campus shared housing, groceries, dining out, local transportation (OC Transpo), entertainment, and personal expenses
interestingFacts:
1. The University of Ottawa is the only bilingual research-intensive university in Canada and the largest bilingual (English-French) university in the world, welcoming nearly 50,000 students from over 150 countries. It was founded in 1848.
  2. uOttawa is ranked 1st in Canada for scholarships and financial aid (Maclean's, Canada's Best Universities 2026) and 5th in Canada in research intensity (Research Infosource 2025), and 5th in Canada for co-op program size.
  3. The uOttawa Computer Engineering program is accredited by the Canadian Engineering Accreditation Board (CEAB) and recognized under the Washington Accord — an international agreement accepting accredited engineering degrees across countries including the USA, UK, and Australia, giving graduates a globally recognized qualification.
